articleBody:
- [ ] Main water shutoff located and verified — Ensures you can quickly cut the water supply if an old isolation valve fails during fixture removal.
- [ ] Hallway and bedroom floor coverings placed — Protects hardwood and carpeting from grit, sharp tile debris, and heavy foot traffic.
- [ ] Vanity and exhaust fan covered with plastic — Keeps fine drywall dust from settling inside drawers or clogging ventilation motors.
- [ ] Rough-in valve access panel identified — Makes disconnecting the mixing valve straightforward without blind cutting into wall cavities.
- [ ] Trash disposal plan and debris staging arranged — Prevents heavy cast-iron tubs or broken mortar pans from cluttering narrow hallways.
- [ ] Finished ceiling heights and replacement footprint measured — Confirms your planned replacement enclosure fits the framing without unexpected framing shifts.
- [ ] Electrical breakers for adjacent bathroom outlets switched off — Reduces electrocution risks when cutting into wet walls where wiring runs near switches.
- [ ] Subfloor moisture inspection tools on hand — Allows immediate assessment of timber decking once the base is lifted.

How to use this checklist:
Work through these items the morning before demolition starts. Ticking off each preparation task guarantees a safe, contained workspace that prevents secondary home damage. If opening the walls reveals rotted framing or plumbing headaches, reach out to Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866.
